drivers.name: price increase (6.2%)
drivers.evidence: Price rose to $12.03 (6.2% above $11.33). Past 2026 weeks at this price: 13 and 24 units (vs baseline 18.5). One past promotion at similar price (2025-06-09) showed x0.87 vs baseline. No past promotion at this price point. Historical price increase likely reduces demand.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.5. The target week has a 6.2% price increase to $12.03, above regular $11.33. Historical data shows no past promotion at this price point. Recent weeks at $12.03 (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw 13 and 24 units—above baseline (18.5), but not unusually so. The 24-unit week (x1.30 vs baseline) is the highest recent sale at elevated price. Past promotions had median x1.52 lift, but noise-adjusted x1.4. However, this is a price increase, not a discount—likely to reduce demand. Price hikes have historically lowered sales (e.g., 2025-06-09: 20% off, x0.87). With no promotion, no event, and a price increase, we expect a slight demand drop. Evidence is thin (one data point at this price), so shrink toward 1.0. The uplift model’s 1.00 is a good starting point but ignores price effect. Adjust down conservatively.

brief:
PRODUCT: Cold & Flu Relief | category Health | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.5 | 5%-95%: 1.4 - 40.9 | 10%-90%: 5.8 - 35.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
